title: Test-root `_ = Module.TypeName;` pins do not force analysis of struct field types or unreferenced functions, so compile errors stay invisible while the target reports green
symptom: `zig build test-lua` exits 0 while two files under src/lua/ contain hard compile errors. `src/lua/instruction_limiter.zig:39` calls `bindings.lua_sethook(...)` and discards its `c_int` result ('value of type c_int ignored'); `src/lua/memory_limiter.zig:13` declares `mutex: std.Thread.Mutex`, which does not exist in Zig 0.16 ('root source file struct Thread has no member named Mutex'). Both errors appear the moment a test actually references `installHook` or constructs a `MemoryLimiter`, but never during `zig build test-lua`.
root_cause: src/lua_test_root.zig pins each file with a bare type or decl reference (`_ = lua.instruction_limiter.InstructionLimiter;`, `_ = lua.memory_limiter.MemoryLimiter;`). Zig resolves a struct's field types lazily: naming the type does not force field-type resolution, so `std.Thread.Mutex` is never looked up. Likewise `_ = someFn;` takes the function's address without requiring its body to be semantically analysed, so a statement-level error inside the body is not reported. `refAllDecls` is explicitly documented as shallow and does not close either gap. The comment in src/lua_test_root.zig claims the pattern was verified by mutation, but the mutation used was a type error inside a function body that IS reached (host_api register()), which does not exercise either of the two blind spots above.
acceptance_criteria: A pin form is adopted that forces both (a) struct field-type resolution and (b) function-body analysis - e.g. `_ = @sizeOf(T);` or `_ = @typeInfo(T).@"struct".fields;` for types, and a real (possibly `if (false)`-guarded but non-comptime-eliminated) call or `_ = &fn;` plus `@TypeOf` usage for functions.

The chosen form is verified by deliberate mutation for BOTH failure shapes: inject a bad field type into a struct, and inject a statement error into an otherwise-unreferenced function; the target must go red in both cases.
The same fix is applied to every src/*_test_root.zig that uses the type-only pin pattern.
tools/lint_test_wiring.py flags a test root whose pins are type-only.
The misleading 'verified by mutation' comment in src/lua_test_root.zig is corrected to state which mutation shapes were actually tested.
notes: Filed per ISSUE_QUEUE.md forwarding rules; not fixed inside WF03-ISS-0169-20260806.

This is the same class as ISS-0133 (26 transition.zig tests wired into no addTest root) and ISS-0147 (src/wasm invisible), but one layer deeper: here the root EXISTS and the pin EXISTS, and the compile error is still not surfaced.
Evidence is reproducible: add `_ = lua.memory_limiter.MemoryLimiter.alloc;` or a real `installHook` call to any target that links src/lua and the two errors appear immediately.
